intro_html: Nose tucked under the tail, back pressed to the nearest edge. A nest dog bed gives a curler walls on every side and something soft to sink into.
description_html:
A nest dog bed is for the dog who settles by curling up: a few turns, nose tucked under a back leg, spine pressed against whatever is closest, which is often the corner of your sofa. Nest and donut dog beds give them that edge all the way round, so whichever way they turn there is a wall to lean into and a soft middle to sink into.

Choosing a nest or donut dog bed

  • If they burrow out of sight: high, deep sides to get behind, on Rydal, Windermere and Elterwater.
  • If they rest a chin on the edge: a rim rather than a wall, on Blea Tarn, Sawrey and Harewood.
  • If they lean hard into the side: Thirlmere's walls are structured felt, so they stand up on their own instead of folding flat night after night.
  • If they come home wet: the Crummock Waterproof Nest keeps high sides under a coated outer that wipes clean.

Then pick the surface they will feel first: sherpa on Windermere and Sawrey, fleece on Rydal, velvet on Harewood, cream bouclé on Blea Tarn, and herringbone outside a lift-out inner cushion on the Crummock Herringbone Nest.

Soft or supportive: what is inside

Many nests are built for softness rather than support. Rydal and Wensleydale are fibre-filled and Blea Tarn soft-filled, yielding rather than firm, and that is the point: they are for sinking into. If your curler is older or stiffer, two nests here put memory foam underneath. Elterwater has a lift-out crumb memory foam cushion with a waterproof layer under the cover. Skelwith closes all four sides around memory foam over an egg-crate layer, and its foam core carries a 5-year no-flatten guarantee, subject to the guarantee terms. For firmer support across a wider choice, see our memory foam dog beds. A bed is for comfort, not a treatment; for a dog in pain, keep talking to your vet.

Sizing a nest around a curled-up dog

Walls eat into the footprint, so measure your dog curled up rather than stretched out, and size up if they fall between two. Sizes run from an XS at 45 × 35cm on Sawrey up to XXL on Rydal. For the smallest curlers, our small dog beds start lower still.

100 nights to see if they settle

Some curlers take a few nights to claim a new nest. Every nest here comes with a 100-night trial from delivery, and if they will not settle in it, we arrange free UK mainland collection and a full refund; one trial per household, and damage and other exclusions apply. Standard UK delivery is free on orders over £40. Read how the trial works.

Nest bed questions

What is the difference between a nest and a donut dog bed?

Mostly the name. Both mean a raised wall all the way round a soft middle; donut usually describes a round one. Wall height and filling matter far more than the label.

Are nest beds washable?

Most have a zipped cover that comes off, and on Blea Tarn, Sawrey, Harewood and Wensleydale it washes at 30°C. Thirlmere's felt structure must not be machine washed, and on the Crummock Waterproof Nest, check the label first, because detergent can affect some waterproof finishes.

My dog curls up but sometimes sprawls. Is a nest still right?

If they stretch out as often as they curl, an edge on three sides may suit them better than four. Our bolster dog beds give them something to lean on without enclosing every side.

Not sure whether yours is a nest dog? The Bed Finder asks how they sleep and tells you.
